title: SonicWall Firewall Unused Access Rule Detection via Hit Counts (SonicWall)
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'SonicWall Firewall Unused Access Rule Detection via Hit Counts (SonicWall)' only. Does not supplant organization-wide SIEM playbooks for unrelated threat classes or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `soc_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `security_infra_sonicwall_firewall_unused_access_rule_detection_` (UC-10.17.1), SOC dashboard panel "Security Infra — SonicWall Firewall Unused Access Rule Detection via Hit Counts (SonicWall)", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:soc_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=netfw` sourcetype='dell:sonicwall:firewall' that satisfy the UC-10.17.1 SPL filters for 'SonicWall Firewall Unused Access Rule Detection via Hit Counts (SonicWall)'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `netfw` / `dell:sonicwall:firewall` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `soc_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-10.17.1.

dataSources: `sourcetype=dell:sonicwall:firewall` with `rule`, `hits` or message-derived hit counters per access rule
spl:
index=netfw sourcetype="dell:sonicwall:firewall" earliest=-30d@d
| where isnotnull(rule) AND match(lower(fw_action),"(?i)allow|accept|permit")
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(hits) as daily_hits by rule, rule_name
| eventstats sum(daily_hits) as total_hits by rule
| where total_hits=0 OR total_hits<5
| dedup rule
| table rule, rule_name, total_hits
description: Many SonicWall policies accrue over years; zero-hit rules may be candidates for removal or indicate logging gaps. Tracking hits proves which controls are actually exercised.
value: Reduces attack surface and simplifies audits by retiring stale rules while validating that critical rules see traffic.
implementation: Enable enhanced firewall logging. If hit counts are not in structured fields, schedule periodic CLI/API exports into a lookup `sonicwall_rule_hits.csv` and join on rule number.
visualization: Bar chart (hits per rule), table (rule id, name, hits, last seen), scatter (rule age vs hits).

detailedImplementation:
Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Dell SonicWall Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 6203)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=dell:sonicwall:firewall into netfw. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`rule, rule_name, total_hits`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
